mainTopic: The signs of a kosher bird: the ברייתא's models of the נשר and the doves, אביי's answer, and רבי חייא's rule that one sign is enough, defended against two challenges
overview: The משנה said the signs of a kosher bird were not stated in the Torah. A ברייתא seems to learn all four signs from Torah examples: the non-kosher נשר, which has none of the signs, and the kosher doves, which have all four. אביי answers that the Torah only gives the examples. Spelling out the signs from them is the work of the חכמים. Then רבי חייא teaches that a bird not on the Torah's list is kosher with even one sign, because the Torah's model of a forbidden bird, the נשר, has none. The גמרא asks why we don't learn from the doves that all four signs are needed. It answers that then the Torah would not need to list the other non-kosher birds. The גמרא then asks why we don't learn from the listed birds with three signs that three are not enough. It answers that then the Torah would not need to name the עורב, which has only two signs. So only the listed birds are forbidden, and any other bird with even one sign is kosher.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns the bird signs from the נשר and the doves
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא compares every bird to the נשר (which has no kosher signs and is טמא) and to the תורין (which have all four signs and are טהור). This seems to show that the signs come from the Torah, against the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the נשר is special because it has no extra toe, no crop, its gizzard can't be peeled, and it claws its food and eats it, and it is non-kosher, so too every bird like it is non-kosher. Doves have an extra toe, a crop, and a gizzard that peels, and they don't claw and eat, and they are kosher. So too every bird like them is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that learns the four signs of a bird from two Torah examples: the non-kosher נשר and the kosher doves. This is brought as a challenge to the משנה, which said the bird signs were not stated in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a comparison in both directions. Any bird that has none of the signs, like the נשר, is טמא, and any bird that has all of them, like the doves, is טהור. If the signs can be learned this way from Torah examples, it sounds like the Torah did give them, which seems to contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird of prey the Torah lists first among the non-kosher birds
An extra toe, the back toe set higher on the foot
Crop, a pouch in the bird's throat where food is stored
A gizzard whose inner lining can be peeled off
Claws its prey and eats it
Doves, kosher birds the Torah permits as קרבנות

phrases.english: Just as the nesher is unique
in that it has no extra toe and no crop
and its gizzard cannot be peeled
and it claws and eats, and it is non-kosher
so too, every bird like it is non-kosher.

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אֶצְבַּע יְתֵרָה וְזֶפֶק
phrases.english: Doves, which have an extra toe and a crop
and whose gizzard can be peeled
and which do not claw and eat, are kosher
so too, every bird like them is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that started before this section, brought against the משנה's statement that the bird signs were not stated in the Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the signs of kosher birds were not stated in the Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns all four signs from the Torah's own examples (נשר and תורין), so the signs seem to come from the Torah after all.

steps.title: אביי: only the explanation of the signs comes from the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה means the details of the signs were not spelled out in the Torah. They are known from the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Their explanation was not stated in the words of the Torah, but in the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by explaining what the משנה really meant when it said the signs were not stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not list the four signs. It only names the נשר and the doves. Figuring out which features of these birds count as the signs is the work of the חכמים, as the ברייתא does. So the ברייתא and the משנה do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Their explanation, meaning the details of what the signs are
What is written in the Torah itself
What the חכמים teach and explain

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah gives the examples (נשר and doves). The חכמים spell out the signs from them. That is why the משנה says the signs were 'not stated.'

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Their explanation was not stated in the words of the Torah
but rather in the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נֶאֱמַר פֵּירוּשָׁן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by reading the משנה's words more precisely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the Torah gives no basis at all for the bird signs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah gives the basis through examples. Only the detailed explanation of the signs comes from the חכמים.

steps.title: רבי חייא: a bird with one kosher sign is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that a bird with even one kosher sign is kosher, because only a bird with no signs, like the נשר, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא teaches: A bird that comes with one sign is kosher, because it is not like the נשר. The Torah means that a bird like the נשר, which has no signs at all, is the one you may not eat. But one that has even one sign, you may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is brought: רבי חייא rules that one kosher sign is enough to make a bird kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא uses the נשר as the model of a non-kosher bird. The נשר has none of the four signs, so the forbidden category is a bird with zero signs. A bird with even one sign is outside that category and is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: One sign of a kosher bird
It is not similar to
It has none at all

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a bird the Torah lists by name as non-kosher. The rule is about an unlisted bird that has only one of the four signs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical standard for an unknown bird: the minimum needed to be kosher is one sign, not all four.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya teaches:
A bird that comes with one sign is kosher
phrases.notes: He is talking about a bird the Torah does not name in its list of non-kosher birds.

phrases.english: because it is not similar to a nesher.
A nesher, which has none at all
that is the one you may not eat

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיכָּא דְּאִית לֵיהּ חַד – תֵּיכוֹל.
phrases.english: but if there is one that has one sign, you may eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: עוֹף הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the נשר model from the ברייתא and draws a practical rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unlisted bird with even one kosher sign is kosher, since only a bird with none, like the נשר, is forbidden.

steps.title: Why not learn from the doves that all four signs are needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we learn from the נשר and not from the doves, which would require all four signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from the doves: just as doves have all four signs, so too here, a bird should not be kosher unless it has all four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא by suggesting we should learn from the kosher doves instead of the non-kosher נשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used two models, the נשר and the doves. If we use the doves as the model, a kosher bird would need all four signs, which is the opposite of רבי חייא's one-sign rule. Why pick the נשר over the doves?

keyTerms.meaning: And let us learn (derive) it from
All four signs

phrases.english: But let us learn from doves:
just as doves have all four signs
so too here as well
a bird is not kosher until it has all four?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's choice of the נשר as the model.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's rule that one sign is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doves are an equally good Torah model, and learning from them would require all four signs.

steps.title: Then why list the other non-kosher birds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if all four signs were needed, the Torah would not have needed to list the other non-kosher birds. So we do not learn from the doves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the rest of the non-kosher birds that the Torah wrote?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חייא by showing that learning from the doves would make part of the Torah's list unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of the listed non-kosher birds has all four signs. If a bird needed all four signs to be kosher, we would already know they are טמא, and the Torah would not need to name them. Since the Torah does name them, a bird can be kosher with fewer than four signs, so we learn from the נשר.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if what you said were true
The rest of the non-kosher birds listed in the Torah
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah
Why do I need it? The Torah does not write extra words

steps.whatToRemember: We learn from the נשר, not the doves, because otherwise the Torah's list of non-kosher birds would be unnecessary. The next step raises one more challenge before רבי חייא's rule is settled.

phrases.english: If so
the rest of the non-kosher birds
that the Merciful One wrote, why do I need them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, שְׁאָר עוֹפוֹת טְמֵאִין דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 and keeps רבי חייא's rule in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The other reading would make part of the Torah unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could learn from the doves that a kosher bird needs all four signs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah's list of other non-kosher birds would then be unnecessary, so we learn from the נשר: a bird not on the Torah's list is forbidden only if it has no signs at all.

steps.title: Why not learn from the listed birds that have three signs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from the other non-kosher birds in the Torah's list. Some of them have three signs and are still forbidden, so any bird with three signs, and all the more so two or one, should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from those other birds: just as they have three signs and we do not eat them, any bird with three signs should not be eaten. All the more so a bird with only two signs or one sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא again. This time it uses a new comparison: the forbidden birds that have three signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 ruled out the doves as a model, but the Torah's list itself has birds with three signs that are still forbidden. If three signs are not enough, then a bird needs all four, and fewer signs would surely not be enough either. This would undo רבי חייא's rule that one sign is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn (by comparing one case to another)
Three (here: three kosher signs)
All the more so; a stronger case follows from a weaker one

phrases.english: But let us learn from them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the other non-kosher birds the Torah lists, some of which have three signs.

phrases.english: just as there, they have three signs and we do not eat them,
so too, any bird with three signs, we should not eat it,
and all the more so a bird with two signs or one sign!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the doves were ruled out as a model, a new model is proposed: the listed birds with three signs.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's rule that one kosher sign is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds in the Torah's list have three signs and are still forbidden, so three signs (and surely fewer) should not be enough.

steps.title: The crow shows that we do not learn from the three-sign birds
steps.stepSummary: If every bird with three signs were forbidden, the Torah would not need to list the עורב, which has only two signs. Since the Torah does list it, we do not learn from the three-sign birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did the Torah need to write the crow? If we do not eat a bird with three signs, do we need to be told about a bird with two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to the עורב in the Torah's list and shows that the suggested comparison would make that word extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not write extra words. If a three-sign bird were forbidden, a two-sign bird like the עורב would surely be forbidden without being named. Since the Torah names the עורב anyway, the rule must be that only the listed birds are forbidden, and any other bird with even one sign is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Crow or raven; a non-kosher bird in the Torah's list, with two kosher signs
Is it necessary? (meaning: obviously not)
Now, if even (introduces a stronger case)

steps.whatToRemember: We do not learn from the doves (Step 5) or from the three-sign birds (this step), because either would make parts of the Torah's list extra. So רבי חייא stands: only the listed birds are forbidden, and any other bird with even one kosher sign is kosher.

phrases.english: If so, the crow,
which the Merciful One wrote in the Torah, why do I need it?
Now, if a bird that has three signs
we do not eat,
is it necessary to say so about one that has only two?
phrases.notes: The crow has only two signs, so it would be forbidden anyway. Naming it would be pointless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, עוֹרֵב, דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by showing that its comparison would make the עורב in the verse extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the proposed comparison would make a word in the Torah extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since three-sign birds are forbidden, any bird missing a sign should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah lists the עורב, so we cannot learn from the three-sign birds. Only listed birds are forbidden; other birds with even one sign are kosher.
